title: Past One
statement: You draw independent uniform random numbers from $[0,1]$ until their running sum exceeds $1$. What is the expected number of draws?
insight: Use E[N] = Σ P(N > n); the event N > n is the first n draws summing to at most 1, a simplex of volume 1/n!.
redHerring: Computing P(N = n) directly by integrating over where the sum crosses 1.
hints: For a positive integer variable, $E[N] = \sum_{n\ge0} P(N>n)$.
$N > n$ means the first $n$ draws sum to at most 1.
The region $x_1+\dots+x_n \le 1$, $x_i\ge0$ is a simplex. What is its volume?
solution:
$N > n$ iff $U_1+\dots+U_n \le 1$, which is the corner simplex of the unit cube with volume $\tfrac1{n!}$.

$E[N] = \sum_{n\ge0} P(N>n) = \sum_{n\ge0}\tfrac1{n!} = e$.
